Williams played [[college basketball]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee Volunteers]]. He was drafted 22nd overall in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]] and reached the [[NBA Finals]] with the team in [[2022 NBA Finals|2022]]. He has also played for the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Williams was elected as the First Vice President of the [[National Basketball Players Association]] in February 2023, replacing [[Andre Iguodala]] in the role.{{Cite web |date=February 18, 2023 |title=NBPA Announces Election Results for Executive Committee Leadership Roles, and Gives Key Updates |url=https://nbpa.com/news/nbpa-announces-election-results-for-executive-committee-leadership-roles-and-gives-key-updates |access-date=August 15, 2023 |website=NBPA.com |language=en}} ==Early life== Born in [[Houston]], Texas, Williams moved to [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] as a child.{{cite web |last=Herbert |first=James |date=November 26, 2019 |title=The Grant Williams experience: How a different kind of rookie is lifting the Celtics up |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-grant-williams-experience-how-a-different-kind-of-rookie-is-lifting-the-celtics-up/ |access-date=May 27, 2023 |work=CBS Sports |quote=...moved from Houston as kids...}} He attended [[Providence Day School]] in Charlotte, where he was teammates with future and fellow NBA player [[Devon Dotson]].{{cite web|last=Bonnell|first=Rick|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/charlotte-hornets/article230444589.html|title= Can Charlotte's Grant Williams overcome that 'tweener' label in NBA draft chase?|work=The Charlotte Observer|date=May 17, 2019|access-date=May 27, 2023}} As a junior in 2014–15, he averaged 18 points, 9.6 rebounds and 2.3 blocks per game while leading the Chargers to a 25–5 overall record. During the summer, Williams joined his AAU team, Team CP3 All-Stars on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] Circuit where he was teammates with fellow top 2016 recruit and future NBA player [[Harry Giles III]].{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/the-grant-williams-experience-how-a-different-kind-of-rookie-is-lifting-the-celtics-up/|title=The Grant Williams experience: How a different kind of rookie is lifting the Celtics up|last=Herbert|first=James|date=November 26, 2019|website=[[CBS Sports]]|access-date=July 21, 2025}} As a senior, Williams averaged 15.8 points, 10.1 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 3.0 blocks per game. Rated a three-star recruit in the class of 2016, Williams committed to [[Tennessee Volunteers men's basketball|Tennessee]] on November 13, 2015.{{cite web |title=Grant Williams [high school] |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Grant-Williams-70078/high-school-123002/ |access-date=May 27, 2023 |publisher=[[247Sports]]}}{{cite web|url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/grant-williams-5388?view=pv|title=Grant Williams, 2016 Power Forward|website=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]]|access-date=June 2, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Grant Williams – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/217191 |access-date=June 2, 2023 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}} ==College career== [[File:Grant Williams 2.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Williams at Tennessee]] Williams was an All-[[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) player as a freshman, sophomore and junior for the Tennessee Volunteers.{{cite web|url=https://utsports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/grant-williams/6755|title=Grant Williams|website=utsports.com|publisher=University of Tennessee, Knoxville|access-date=May 27, 2023|archive-date=June 3, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190603122745/https://utsports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=6755|url-status=live}} He was awarded back-to-back [[Southeastern Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|SEC Player of the Year]] honors for the [[2017–18 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2017–18]] and [[2018–19 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|2018–19]] seasons, becoming the first player to do so since [[Corliss Williamson]] in 1995.{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Mike |date=March 6, 2018 |title=UT Vols basketball sweeps |url=https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2018/03/06/tennessee-vols-basketball-rick-barnes-sec-coach-grant-williams-player-year-admiral-schofield/394055002/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190507115043/https://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/mens-basketball/2018/03/06/tennessee-vols-basketball-rick-barnes-sec-coach-grant-williams-player-year-admiral-schofield/394055002/ |archive-date=May 7, 2019 |access-date=April 24, 2019 |website=Knoxville News Sentinel}} Williams led Tennessee as a third seed in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]] and second seed in the [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019 NCAA tournament]]. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2019–2023)=== Williams was selected with the 22nd overall draft pick by the Boston Celtics in the 2019 NBA draft.{{cite web |date=June 21, 2019 |title=Celtics Draft Langford, Williams, Edwards & Waters |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-draft-langford-williams-edwards-waters |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190623092312/https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-draft-langford-williams-edwards-waters |archive-date=June 23, 2019 |access-date=June 21, 2019 |publisher=NBA}} On July 11, 2019, the Celtics announced that they had signed him to a four-year, $11.8 million rookie-scale contract.{{cite web |last=George |first=Kyle |date=July 11, 2019 |title=Celtics Sign Pair of First-Round Draft Picks Langford, Williams officially join Celtics |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-pair-first-round-draft-picks |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712062822/https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-pair-first-round-draft-picks |archive-date=July 12, 2019 |access-date=July 11, 2019 |publisher=NBA}} On October 23, 2019, Williams made his professional debut, coming off the bench in a loss to the [[2019–20 Philadelphia 76ers season|Philadelphia 76ers]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160630|title=76ers top Celtics 107–93 in 1st battle of East favorites|date=October 23, 2019|publisher=ESPN|access-date=October 23, 2019|archive-date=October 24, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191024035916/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160630|url-status=live}} On December 4, 2019, he made his first career start in a winning effort against the [[2019–20 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]].{{cite web|title=Grant Williams to make first career start vs. Heat|date=December 5, 2019|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/04/grant-williams-to-make-first-career-start-vs-heat/|access-date=June 28, 2021|archive-date=June 28, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210628225500/https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2019/12/04/grant-williams-to-make-first-career-start-vs-heat/|url-status=live}} In an effort to garner support for teammates making the [[2020 NBA All-Star Game]], Williams pledged to dye his hair pink if [[Jaylen Brown]], [[Jayson Tatum]] and [[Kemba Walker]] all received a selection.{{Cite web|url=https://boston.cbslocal.com/2020/01/14/grant-williams-celtics-all-stars-dye-hair-pink-kemba-walker-jayson-tatum-jaylen-brown-nba/|title=Grant Williams Will Dye His Hair Pink If Celtics Teammates Make NBA All-Star Team|date=January 14, 2020|website=CBS Boston|language=en-US|access-date=January 16, 2020|archive-date=January 15, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200115142414/https://boston.cbslocal.com/2020/01/14/grant-williams-celtics-all-stars-dye-hair-pink-kemba-walker-jayson-tatum-jaylen-brown-nba/|url-status=live}} However, Williams did not do so as Brown did not make the team. Williams finished his rookie season averaging just over 15 minutes per game in 69 games, 3.4 points per game and 2.6 rebounds per game.{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willigr01/gamelog/2020|title=Grant Williams 2019–20 Game Log|access-date=June 28, 2021|archive-date=August 15, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210815042159/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/willigr01/gamelog/2020|url-status=live}} Upon completion of the [[2020–21 NBA season]], Williams' second season in the league, he slightly increased his averages in all major statistical categories. He finished the season averaging just over 18 minutes per game, 4.7 points per game and 2.8 rebounds per game.{{Cite web |title=Grant Williams {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1629684/grant-williams/ |access-date=February 17, 2024 |website=nba.com |language=en}} On March 21, 2022, Williams scored a then career-high 20 points in a win against the [[2021–22 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]].{{Cite web|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2022/03/22/nba-boston-celtics-grant-batman-williams-highlights/|title=Grant Williams highlights: Celtics forward gets 20 points, 10 boards vs. OKC Thunder (3/21)|access-date=April 1, 2022}} He finished the [[2021–22 NBA season]] with career-best averages with over 24 minutes per game, 7.8 points per game and 3.6 rebounds per game. On May 15, Williams scored a career-high 27 points in a decisive game 7 win over the [[2021–22 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]] in the Eastern Conference Semifinals. His performance was highlighted by a 7-for-18 mark from three point range, records for both made threes and three attempts in an NBA game 7. Williams helped the Celtics reach the [[2022 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], but lost to the [[2021–22 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] in six games. On October 26, 2022, Williams was suspended for one game without pay for making contact with a game official during a 102–120 loss to the [[2022–23 Chicago Bulls season|Chicago Bulls]] two days earlier.{{Cite web |date=October 26, 2022 |title=Celtics' Grant Williams suspended |url=https://pr.nba.com/grant-williams-suspended-10-26-22/ |access-date=November 21, 2022 |publisher=NBA}} On March 6, 2023, Williams missed two critical free throws in the final seconds, costing his team the victory. Adding to the disappointment, Williams yelled at [[2022–23 Cleveland Cavaliers season|Cavs]] shooting guard [[Donovan Mitchell]] before the shots that he would make them both. Despite his pledge, both shots missed their mark, resulting in a 118–114 loss in overtime. Williams was attacked online with fans naming him "Not him".{{Cite web |last=Singh |first=Sanjesh |date=March 7, 2023 |title=Grant Williams misses game-winning FTs, claimed he'd 'make both' |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/boston/celtics/celtics-grant-williams-misses-game-winning-free-throws-claimed-hed-make-both |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=nbcsports.com}} On May 19, 2023, during game 2 of the [[2023 NBA playoffs#(2) Boston Celtics vs. (8) Miami Heat|Eastern Conference Finals]] versus the [[2022–23 Miami Heat season|Miami Heat]], Williams had nine points, two rebounds, two assists and one block in 26 minutes off the bench.{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202305190BOS.html|title=2023 NBA Eastern Conference Finals Game 2: Miami Heat at Boston Celtics Box Score, May 19, 2023|publisher=Basketball Reference|access-date=May 20, 2023}} After Williams scored on a three-pointer to give Boston a 96–87 lead with 6:37 left, he mouthed some words to Heat forward [[Jimmy Butler]] while in transition to defense. Williams then fouled Butler on a made basket.{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5ldCRGbOAHk|title=Jimmy Butler & Grant Williams Get Into It|author=Bleacher Report|via=YouTube|access-date=May 20, 2023|date=May 19, 2023}} They then confronted each other verbally, resulting in technical fouls being issued to both players.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/celtics-vs-heat-grant-williams-poked-the-wrong-bear-and-jimmy-butler-ate-him-alive-in-bostons-game-2-loss/|title=Celtics vs. Heat: Grant Williams poked the wrong bear, and Jimmy Butler ate him alive in Boston's Game 2 loss |work=CBS Sports|last=Botkin|first=Brad|date=May 20, 2023|access-date=May 20, 2023}}{{cite web |last=Hightower |first=Kyle |date=May 20, 2023 |title=Celtics pay price for Williams dust up, Tatum's cold finish in East finals Game 2 loss |url=https://apnews.com/article/celtics-nba-playoffs-2023-a063c033eb7735592e383555a50316fc |access-date=May 20, 2023 |website=apnews.com |agency=Associated Press}} Butler said that the incident energized him; the Heat finished the game on a 24–9 run and won 111–105.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37689088 |title=Heat's Jimmy Butler: Exchange with Grant Williams fueled me |publisher=ESPN|last=Friedell|first=Nick |date=May 20, 2023|access-date=May 20, 2023}} ===Dallas Mavericks (2023–2024)=== On July 12, 2023, Williams was traded to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in a sign-and-trade agreement, signing a four-year, $53.3 million contract.{{cite web |last=Sefko |first=Eddie |date=July 12, 2023 |title=Popular, young and talented Williams arrives to Mavericks |url=https://www.mavs.com/grant-williams-arrives |access-date=July 12, 2023 |publisher=Dallas Mavericks}} He made his debut for the Mavericks on October 25, 2023, in a 126–119 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |date=October 25, 2023 |title=Mavericks spoil Victor Wembanyama's NBA debut, beat the Spurs 126–119 in the teams' opener |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401584701 |access-date=October 25, 2023 |publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} ===Charlotte Hornets (2024–present)=== On February 8, 2024, Williams was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] alongside [[Seth Curry]] and a 2027 first-round pick in exchange for [[P. J. Washington]] and two future second-round picks.{{cite web|title=Hornets Acquire Seth Curry, Grant Williams And A 2027 First-Round Pick From Dallas|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-acquire-seth-curry-grant-williams-and-a-2027-first-round-pick-from-dallas|website=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2024|access-date=February 8, 2024}} On November 23, 2024, Williams suffered a season-ending torn [[anterior cruciate ligament]], [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]], and other ligaments in the right knee during a game against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. Williams was driving to the basket late in the fourth quarter, losing his footing after bumping into Bucks center [[Brook Lopez]], where he landed awkwardly with a long step and collapsed onto the court. He was helped off the court and did not return to the game.{{Cite web |last=Quinn |first=Sam |date=November 24, 2024 |title=Grant Williams injury: Hornets forward out for rest of season after multiple tears in right knee, per report |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/grant-williams-injury-hornets-forward-out-for-rest-of-season-after-multiple-tears-in-right-knee-per-report/ |access-date=November 24, 2024 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}} On January 10, 2026, Williams officially made his return from injury, playing 13 minutes off the bench during a 150–95 victory over the [[2025–26 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web|title=Former Celtics Forward Returns From Injury Following Near 14-Month
